audit_findings.title: The valuation assigns a 2026 acquisition to FY2025
audit_findings.magnitude: 48 restaurants and $8.7 million consideration; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-FY2025 acquisition changes the operating perimeter, future OE, reinvestment needs and potentially working capital, while the anchor remains based on the pre-acquisition business.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, 62 franchise groups (32 domestic and 30 international) operated 1,520 Applebee’s franchised restaurants and we owned 59 Applebee's restaurants acquired from franchisees, of which 47 were acquired in November 2024 and 12 were acquired in May 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The date error is demonstrated: FY2025 ended December 28, 2025, whereas the 48 restaurants were acquired June 1, 2026. They represented 35.3% of the 136 company-owned restaurants reported after acquisition. Whether they increase or decrease sustainable OE is unresolved, but their scale is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Correct the perimeter description and rerun using post-acquisition revenue, expenses, capex, working capital and financing from the 2026 filings, without assigning the acquisition to FY2025.

audit_findings.title: The cash addition may include operating float rather than distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $97.5 million, equal to $6.78 per share and 22.5% of $434 million base equity value; $85.4 million was in depository accounts including IHOP advertising and gift-card cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash is added directly in the equity bridge even though some may be required to settle gift cards, advertising expenditures, debt reserves or ordinary liquidity needs.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash held related to IHOP advertising funds and the Company's gift card programs is not considered to be restricted cash as there are no restrictions on the use of these funds.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that cash composition includes operating-program funds, but do not establish the surplus portion. The entire $97.5 million addition is large enough to change the conclusion; the contemporaneous $158.1 million gift-card liability reinforces that legal unrestrictedness alone does not establish distributability.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $97.5 million by program and liability, determine minimum operating and acquisition liquidity, and rerun the bridge with only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may understate the current debt-service run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 six-month net interest expense was $43.8 million, or $87.6 million annualized, versus $78.0 million in FY2025; computed gap $9.6 million pre-tax annually
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest expense remains in equity-level OE, so a partial-year refinancing rate understates recurring interest and inflates the OE anchor if not normalized.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense, net, increased $5.9 million in 2025, primarily due to the refinancing of our Series 2025-1 6.720% Fixed Rate Senior Secured Notes, Class A-2 at a higher interest rate and an increase to the principal, partially offset by a decrease in the Credit Facility interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The run-rate mismatch is demonstrated by the filed interest expense: the annualized 2026 amount is $9.6 million above FY2025, although part of the increase reflects lower interest income. That gap is 37.9% of the $25.3 million anchor before considering taxes, so it is reasonably capable of changing value. The supplied filings show $1.2 billion face debt at both December 2025 and June 2026, so increased face debt after FY2025 is not demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct gross interest expense and interest income separately using the $500 million 7.824% notes, $600 million 6.720% notes, $100 million facility, issuance-cost amortization and 2026 cash balances; then rerun OE with the normalized after-tax interest amount.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling appears to double-count issued restricted stock
audit_findings.magnitude: 14.378011 million valuation shares exceed the July 2026 cover count of 12.659150 million by 1.718861 million, or 13.6%; using the cover count alone would raise base value from $30.17 to $34.28 per share, a $4.11 difference
audit_findings.mechanism: An overstated fully diluted denominator depresses every scenario's value per share without changing total equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company utilizes treasury stock or issues new shares from its authorized but unissued share pool when vested stock options are exercised, restricted stock awards are granted and when restricted stock units vest.
audit_findings.explanation: Double-counting is not yet proved award by award, but the filed policy confirms restricted stock is issued when granted, and the denominator difference is sufficient to change the conclusion relative to the $31.68 market price. Some incremental RSUs or other dilution must still be included, so $4.11 per share is a scale bound rather than an established correction.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the July 26 cover count to restricted-stock and RSU roll-forwards, remove awards already included in outstanding shares, add only genuinely incremental unissued awards and options, and rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Lease guarantees are contingent claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $79.4 million filed maximum exposure at June 28, 2026, equal to $5.52 per valuation share and 18.3% of base equity value; probability-weighted amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Realized guarantee payments would reduce OE or require an equity-bridge deduction, subject to indemnity recoveries and timing.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluding unexercised option periods, the Company's potential liability for future payments under these leases were $83.1 million and $90.5 million as of December 28, 2025 and December 29, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual maximum is material in scale, but the filing reports no presently recognized material guarantee liability and does not establish probable defaults. This is therefore a contingent, forward-looking exposure rather than a demonstrated omission from current value.
audit_findings.action: Monitor guaranteed franchisee defaults, closures, credit quality, collateral and indemnification recoverability; rerun with a probability-weighted claim if filed developments make payment probable or estimable.

audit_findings.title: The depressed anchor may capitalize a nonrecurring impairment forever
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.0 million impairment, equal to 114.6% of the $25.3 million OE anchor; sustainable net adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in OE, the one-time noncash charge depresses the anchor and all forecast cash flows; the underlying Fuzzy's deterioration may instead require lower sustainable OE or growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In the fourth quarter of 2025, the Company determined the Fuzzy's tradename intangible asset was impaired and recorded a $29.0 million noncash impairment charge.
audit_findings.explanation: The impairment and its size are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether it was retained in the OE reconciliation. Because the charge exceeds the anchor, retention could materially understate value. Mechanical removal could overstate value if the forecast does not separately reflect weaker royalties, closures and reinvestment.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $29.0 million charge through the FY2025 OE reconciliation; if retained, remove the accounting charge and separately model filed evidence of sustainable Fuzzy's economics before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.7 million FY2019 residual computed from $30.8 million representing 72.5% of filed D&A; FY2025 effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic D&A left as an expense reduces historical OE and could reduce the latest-year anchor if a similar residual exists in FY2025.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $30.8m (72.5% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment cannot overstate value, but the cited amount concerns FY2019. Because the current anchor is the $25.3 million latest-year OE rather than the higher $52 million trend, correcting FY2019 alone would not increase the anchor. The record does not quantify or classify the FY2025 residual, so present materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 filed D&A by asset and business function, identify any eligible non-economic residual, and rerun only the latest-year OE and anchor if filed support exists.
